newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end quiet day slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end quiet day slightly higher.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended slightly higher after a very quiet session, with many players on hold before late-week data.
Traders termed the market well-supported, but said corporate supply woes and upcoming retail and producer price data kept buyers wary.
September Treasury bond futures traded in a tight range between 110-13/32 and 110-23/32. Support at Tuesday's 110-12/32 low and resistance at 111-00 went unchallenged.
Furthmore, a Federal Reserve coupon pass did little to stir market interest, traders said.
"It doesn't look like people were willing to do much here," said Don Pullen, bond trading floor manager with E.D. and F Man. "We're just waiting for tomorrow."
He said the market was supported by the notion Thursday and Friday data would show only a modest uptick in retail sales and that inflation was still under control.
"I think the whole week traders thought these numbers would be bond friendly, so that is still the tone here," Pullen said.
A Reuters poll of economists showed an average forecast of up 0.4 percent overall in U.S. May retail sales.
The average forecast for sales excluding autos was up 0.3 percent. On Friday, May producer prices will be reported, and are forecast up 0.1 percent both overall and excluding food and energy.
Traders said debt futures showed little conviction in either direction Wednesday. In fact, several noted that no key technical levels in T-bonds or in the short end had been violated this week.
"It feels so mixed," a T-bond futures trader said. "I think we're going to get weak data, but the question is, is it priced in already?"

A Eurodollar trader said recent action in the short end shapes up to be a minor bull flag formation, which could portend small technical gains. But he pegged December Euro resistance at 93.88, not far above the market.

At the close, September T-bonds were up 2/32 at 110-19/32, 10-yr notes rose 1/32 to 108-4/32, munis rose 10/32 to 118-17/32, Sept bills were up 0.015 point at 94.680, Dec Euros rose 0.005 to 93.815. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
